pairs.why: A's saddle sits over a fence rail held up by a visible post, with the stirrup hanging naturally; B's saddle rests on a single rail with no supports, and its two stirrups bunch up awkwardly under one flap.
B's labeled key grid follows the tilt of the calculator face like the real card does, while A's keys are blank, so it couldn't work as a calculator.
A is a wall clock seen face-on against the wall, like the real card; B balances a round clock on its rim on a floor seen from a different angle, so it couldn't stay upright.
A's X-legs, armrests and seat join into one folding frame; in B, the front seat bar sticks out past the frame and the leg bars don't connect clearly to the back posts.
Both hang from a clamp, but A's yoke and pivot knobs line up cleanly with the truss and the lamp barrel, while B's thin stem and yoke look less securely joined.
B's X-braced legs, armrests and seat form one connected folding frame; in A, the armrests and the cross legs meet the seat at unclear points.
A hangs from a single clamp with the yoke pivots aligned to the barrel; B's two-clamp yoke sits on a steeply tilted truss whose angle doesn't match the lamp's.
A's clock hangs flat on the wall like the real card; B's round clock stands on its rim on a floor drawn from another angle, with nothing holding it up.
